jobs.description:
UNITED WAY BC IS PROUD TO BE RECOGNIZED AS ONE OF CANADA'S TOP 100 EMPLOYERS FOR 2026 !

ABOUT US – WHY WE’RE HERE:

Across British Columbia, communities are facing urgent and complex social challenges. United Way BC is committed to delivering lasting, community-driven impact in partnership with diverse populations across the province including Indigenous communities whose territories we live and work on. From Vancouver Island to the Lower Mainland, and across the Thompson Nicola Cariboo, Southern Interior, Trail and District, and East Kootenay regions, we walk alongside communities to create meaningful and equitable change. 

Our mission
is to strengthen vital connections that support people in need in our communities. 

Our vision
is to create a healthy, caring and inclusive community. 

How do we deliver on our mission and vision – by delivering resources and support for those who need it most, and by living our values of being collaborative, compassionate, strategic, responsive, accountable, and inspiring. 

For a more in-depth to look into our work and programs, please visit: www.uwbc.ca.

ABOUT YOU:
You're a strategic technology and data leader with at least seven years of progressively responsible experience, including three years leading teams. You've developed enterprise technology and data strategies and overseen cloud, applications, cybersecurity, BI and data governance. You've also led change and adoption of new tools, including AI and automation, with the right safeguards. You manage budgets and vendors with confidence, and you advise senior leaders in clear, practical terms. As an inclusive, collaborative leader, you build trusted relationships across a hybrid, multi-location organization. A degree in a related field, or equivalent experience, is required. Experience in nonprofit, public-sector or unionized settings, and with platforms such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI and Salesforce, is an asset.

JOB PURPOSE:
The Director, Information Technology & Business Intelligence is UWBC’s most senior technology professional and the principal partner to the Chief Financial & Technology Officer (CFTO) on all technology and data matters. Accountable to the CFTO, the Director is trusted to set strategy, manage budgets and run operations for Information Technology (IT) and Business Intelligence (BI), and to lead the team and external partners in delivering reliable services, trusted information and effective technology adoption.

The Director sets priorities, standards and resource allocations; decides on vendors, risk mitigation and staffing; recommends enterprise strategies and significant investments to the CFTO; and escalates matters with significant organizational, financial, security, privacy or reputational implications. Working with senior leadership and with finance, fundraising, community impact and regional teams, the Director champions innovation while balancing provincial consistency, regional needs, staff capacity and responsible stewardship.

The role requires broad knowledge of technology strategy and governance, cybersecurity and privacy, cloud and enterprise applications, BI and data stewardship, and technology financial and vendor management, together with the judgment to direct specialists and external partners. It also requires inclusive leadership of change, innovation and people, and the ability to build trusted cross-functional relationships.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategy and advisory

Lead an integrated technology, data and digital strategy and adaptable roadmap that drives innovation, aligning investments, architecture and governance with organizational priorities, capacity, cost, risk and long-term value.

Advise senior leadership on significant technology, data, cybersecurity and digital opportunities and risks, translating complex issues into clear options and recommendations.

Agree priorities with business leaders, retaining business ownership of process changes and outcomes and escalating unresolved priorities or material risks.

Champion innovation by assessing and introducing technologies, automation and AI through practical use cases, controlled pilots and measured results, with privacy, security, human oversight and monitoring.

Contribute to organizational planning and represent UWBC with technology partners and external stakeholders.

IT operations and enterprise systems

Oversee reliable, secure and integrated infrastructure, cloud, networks, devices, telecommunications, enterprise applications and end-user services against defined service standards, measured by service availability and incident response times.

Govern technology and application selection, integration and lifecycle management, with clear business and technical ownership, documentation, and asset, licensing, access and configuration controls.

Cybersecurity, risk and resilience

Lead cybersecurity and technology risk management, including identity and access controls, secure use, risk assessment, mitigation and reporting across operations and investments, measured by security and recovery readiness, including tested recovery.

Ensure recovery, backup and incident-response capabilities are documented, tested and aligned with business continuity priorities.

Lead responses to significant disruptions and cybersecurity incidents, advising senior leadership on material risks.

With designated organizational leaders, define technology responsibilities for privacy, information management and enterprise risk, including retention and disposal, third-party data handling and privacy-incident escalation, in line with applicable privacy legislation such as BC’s Personal Information Protection Act.

Business intelligence, analytics and data governance

Deliver the BI and analytics plan with business owners, prioritizing dashboards, reporting and forecasting that support planning, operations, fundraising and community-impact decisions, measured by BI usage and data quality.

Oversee data architecture, integration and governance, setting ownership, quality and access standards that protect sensitive information.

Build data literacy through practical training so teams can use reports, shared definitions and reliable information in decisions and evaluation.

Projects and change

Lead cross-functional initiatives collaboratively, with clear executive sponsorship, business ownership, outcomes, scope, resources, milestones and success measures, delivering on time and cost.

Resolve competing operational, technical, financial, security and stakeholder needs, developing new approaches where existing practices fall short.

Co-design improvements with staff and business owners, leading readiness, process redesign, communication, training and post-launch support, sequenced to staff capacity to sustain adoption of new systems and tools.

Evaluate outcomes with business owners against agreed adoption, service, staff-time, data-quality, cost and risk measures, and recommend changes where benefits are not sustained.

People leadership

Lead integrated IT and BI functions, setting clear responsibilities, priorities, service expectations and performance objectives and allocating capacity across operations and initiatives.

Coach employees and leaders, and oversee recruitment, performance, engagement, development, succession and knowledge continuity.

Build an inclusive, collaborative, accountable and service-oriented culture and strong working relationships across UWBC, measured by team engagement and retention.

Financial and vendor management

Manage operating and capital budgets, project costs, capacity and funding needs, measured by budget performance against plan. Recommend significant investments and improve value from licensing, subscriptions and services.

Oversee vendors, consultants and managed services, including selection, contracts, renewals and performance, with corrective action where needed.

Ensure technology procurement and expenditures comply with organizational policies.

Qualifications and requirements: Education

University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Data/Analytics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant professional experience.

Advanced education or certification in technology governance, cybersecurity, data management, cloud or project management is an asset.

Experience

At least seven years of progressively responsible technology, digital or BI/data experience, including three years leading technology, data or multidisciplinary teams.

Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology, digital or data strategies and overseeing operations, cloud, applications, cybersecurity, technology risk, BI and data governance.

Demonstrated experience leading technology implementations and cross-functional change, including AI or automation, through staff engagement, process redesign, training and sustained adoption, with measurable benefits and safeguards.

Experience managing budgets, contracts, vendors and external service providers.

Assets: experience in complex, multi-location, nonprofit, public-sector or unionized environments; and experience integrating or deriving insight from CRM, financial or ERP systems and modern data platforms, such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI, Salesforce and Microsoft data warehouse technologies.

working conditions:

Works with confidential, sensitive and security-related organizational information, balancing concurrent strategic, operational and stakeholder priorities and making timely decisions on emerging risks and issues.

Works in a hybrid, multi-location environment with occasional travel within British Columbia.

Occasional work outside regular business hours may be required in connection with significant system implementations, service disruptions or cybersecurity incidents.

Other related duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
About Nuvollo

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Toronto, Nuvollo Corp has established itself as a leader in delivering secure, high-performance cloud and IT infrastructure solutions to businesses across North America. A fast-growing cloud company focused on managing and operating business critical systems such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) requiring high availability, secure and predictable environments. Nuvollo’s commitment to reliability, compliance, and customer-centric service has allowed it to build long-standing relationships with clients in highly regulated industries such as healthcare, finance, and professional services.

In August 2025, Nuvollo expanded its North American platform through the acquisition of a U.S.-based business, strengthening its market presence and broadening its service capabilities. As the company continues its strong growth trajectory, Nuvollo is focused on strengthening its leadership team and building the internal capabilities needed to scale. A key priority is enhancing its financial management, strategic planning, and reporting functions to support continued expansion, integration activities, and investor reporting.

Snowdon Partners
, a leading mid-market private investment firm, has recently made an important investment in Nuvollo, and has partnered with them to launch a search for a Director of Finance
. This role represents a unique opportunity to build and lead a finance function in a growing private equity-backed business.

The Role

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, working closely with the private equity CFO, and managing a team of four (4) direct reports, the Director of Finance serves as the company’s financial quarterback and is a key member of the leadership team, participating in strategic discussions and supporting all areas of the business.

The ideal candidate will not only build and implement accurate and timely financial reports, tailored KPIs, and actionable insights to drive the business forward, but will also develop best-in-class budgeting and forecasting tools, and lead multi-currency, multi-country consolidation, an exciting opportunity to shape the company’s financial reporting capabilities. Given the recent private equity investment in the company, this role will operate at a slightly faster pace than traditional director of finance positions, providing direct exposure to the private equity CFO and investors, and offering genuine participation in strategic decision-making.

Who You Are

The successful candidate is a hands-on accounting and finance leader with extensive experience in multi-currency, international consolidation and a strong track record of building scalable financial processes. You know that growth and management start with getting the basics right-timely, accurate reporting and robust controls – but you also understand that true financial leadership extends to driving strategy, supporting growth, and navigating complex international operations. You are energized by change, resilient in the face of challenges, and skilled at identifying which initiatives will deliver lasting impact.

You will dive into Nuvollo’s financial results, lead consolidation across multiple currencies and international entities, and work closely with the team to develop KPIs, reporting frameworks, best-in-class budgeting and forecasting tools. Your experience supporting acquisitions, integration initiatives, or international cross-selling efforts will allow you to contribute meaningfully to strategic growth opportunities as Nuvollo continues to scale. You show up as your authentic self, approaching new challenges with purpose, energy, and enthusiasm, and are motivated by the opportunity to shape Nuvollo’s financial future in a dynamic, fast-growing environment.

What You Will Build

Reporting and controls:
using data, you will build actionable insights and enhance our executive team’s visibility and decision-making.
Manage the company’s financial accounts.
Identify, create, and implement financial controls.
Develop Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and create management dashboards to allow management to track performance of critical data points.
Prepare annual budgets and update with actual results throughout the year.
Prepare monthly and quarterly reporting packages, including year-to-date performance and projected year-end results.
Prepare compliance reports and financial packages for lender partners.
Become the “go-to” leader internally for financial performance data.

Financial accounting and cash management:
as our financial quarterback, you will ensure our accounting is always up to date and our cash position is optimized, balancing growth requirements and opportunistic capital deployment with real-time cash constraints.
Compile, close, and prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow), as well as discussion materials presenting key performance trends for management decision-making.
Verify staff accountants’ work to ensure quality of data entry to the general ledger.
Prepare backup schedules for annual third-party accounting audit procedures.
Verify weekly bank reconciliations and take necessary actions to proactively manage the company’s cash flow.
Develop cash flow forecasts to manage cash requirements for growth investments.
Track equipment purchases, improvements, dispositions, and work with operations teams to optimize fixed asset management.
Manage and oversee working capital accounts, including invoicing and receivables, supplier payments, and prepaid expenses.

International operations & growth enablement:
as Nuvollo continues to expand, you will strengthen our ability to manage international growth and support sales.
Lead multi-currency, multi-entity consolidation and reporting.
Ensure compliance with international accounting standards and local regulations in jurisdictions where Nuvollo operates.
Build scalable reporting processes that allow management to track performance across countries and business entities.
Partner with leaders to provide financial analysis supporting international cross-selling initiatives and expansion opportunities.
Contribute financial integration support for acquisitions in new markets.

Information technology:
while reviewing and assessing processes, you will integrate technology into our financial practices to help Nuvollo become more effective as an organization.
Ensure integration of ERP and CRM solutions with our accounting systems in collaboration with the finance group of Snowdon Partners.
Act as key liaison during implementation of new software solutions and lead change management with the Nuvollo team.
Identify and implement a scalable ERP platform.
Identify and implement automation solutions for recurring accounting activities, such as A/P automation, payroll single-point management, and field expense tracking.

High-performing team:
you will lead a strong team of accounting staff.
Build, foster, coach, and mentor a highly engaged accounting team.
Create an environment to develop, attract, and retain top talent.
Introduce best practices and instill a mindset of continuous improvement.

Strategic planning:
as the company’s finance leader, you will have the mandate to integrate long-term thinking into Nuvollo’s financial management practices, ensuring soundness and scalability are part of our ethos.
Support the senior leadership team in developing the company’s strategic plans.
Lead long-term financial planning, including forecasting and budgeting.
Performance management: analyze and make recommendations regarding service lines, staff utilization, operations, volumes, and profitability.
Provide executive leadership and financial oversight for procurement, and vendor management activities, ensuring purchasing strategies, supplier relationships, and spending decisions align with the company's financial, operational, and strategic objectives.

Tax management:
you will maintain our standing with the relevant tax authorities.
Work with the company’s external accountants to prepare and file year-end tax declarations.
Prepare and file other tax declarations as required.
Prepare documentation for and provide support during government audits.

Your Profile

You hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting and a Canadian CPA designation, with a minimum of 8 years experience in a similar leadership role.
You demonstrate a strong understanding of GAAP/ASPE and have consistently applied superior technical accounting knowledge in prior roles.
You have prior experience working within an IT/MSP business (preferred).
You have a solid track record of identifying, implementing, and optimizing technology, through software implementations or process upgrades.
You possess excellent communication skills with an impactful presentation style.
You are highly reliable, rigorous, and organized, with exceptional attention to detail.
You can manage multiple projects simultaneously, adapt quickly to change, and perform well under pressure.
You lead with positivity, inspiring your team and fostering strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
You embrace technological to improve processes and drive automation.
You care about your colleagues and consistently strive to do the right thing.
You are naturally curious, eager to take on challenges, and thrive in dynamic, fast-growing environments.
You reject “the way we’ve always done it” mindset and embrace continuous improvement.

What We Offer

A high-performance environment where you will grow and take your career to the next level.
An intensely collaborative team and culture, where decision velocity and results are primary markers of success, but where people are at the heart of it all.
A market-leading mindset where creative solutions are not only encouraged but rewarded.
Competitive compensation & comprehensive benefits package.

Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

ABOUT YOU:
You're a strategic technology and data leader with at least seven years of progressively responsible experience, including three years leading teams. You've developed enterprise technology and data strategies and overseen cloud, applications, cybersecurity, BI and data governance. You've also led change and adoption of new tools, including AI and automation, with the right safeguards. You manage budgets and vendors with confidence, and you advise senior leaders in clear, practical terms. As an inclusive, collaborative leader, you build trusted relationships across a hybrid, multi-location organization. A degree in a related field, or equivalent experience, is required. Experience in nonprofit, public-sector or unionized settings, and with platforms such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI and Salesforce, is an asset.

JOB PURPOSE:
The Director, Information Technology & Business Intelligence is UWBC’s most senior technology professional and the principal partner to the Chief Financial & Technology Officer (CFTO) on all technology and data matters. Accountable to the CFTO, the Director is trusted to set strategy, manage budgets and run operations for Information Technology (IT) and Business Intelligence (BI), and to lead the team and external partners in delivering reliable services, trusted information and effective technology adoption.

The Director sets priorities, standards and resource allocations; decides on vendors, risk mitigation and staffing; recommends enterprise strategies and significant investments to the CFTO; and escalates matters with significant organizational, financial, security, privacy or reputational implications. Working with senior leadership and with finance, fundraising, community impact and regional teams, the Director champions innovation while balancing provincial consistency, regional needs, staff capacity and responsible stewardship.

The role requires broad knowledge of technology strategy and governance, cybersecurity and privacy, cloud and enterprise applications, BI and data stewardship, and technology financial and vendor management, together with the judgment to direct specialists and external partners. It also requires inclusive leadership of change, innovation and people, and the ability to build trusted cross-functional relationships.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategy and advisory

Lead an integrated technology, data and digital strategy and adaptable roadmap that drives innovation, aligning investments, architecture and governance with organizational priorities, capacity, cost, risk and long-term value.

Advise senior leadership on significant technology, data, cybersecurity and digital opportunities and risks, translating complex issues into clear options and recommendations.

Agree priorities with business leaders, retaining business ownership of process changes and outcomes and escalating unresolved priorities or material risks.

Champion innovation by assessing and introducing technologies, automation and AI through practical use cases, controlled pilots and measured results, with privacy, security, human oversight and monitoring.

Contribute to organizational planning and represent UWBC with technology partners and external stakeholders.

IT operations and enterprise systems

Oversee reliable, secure and integrated infrastructure, cloud, networks, devices, telecommunications, enterprise applications and end-user services against defined service standards, measured by service availability and incident response times.

Govern technology and application selection, integration and lifecycle management, with clear business and technical ownership, documentation, and asset, licensing, access and configuration controls.

Cybersecurity, risk and resilience

Lead cybersecurity and technology risk management, including identity and access controls, secure use, risk assessment, mitigation and reporting across operations and investments, measured by security and recovery readiness, including tested recovery.

Ensure recovery, backup and incident-response capabilities are documented, tested and aligned with business continuity priorities.

Lead responses to significant disruptions and cybersecurity incidents, advising senior leadership on material risks.

With designated organizational leaders, define technology responsibilities for privacy, information management and enterprise risk, including retention and disposal, third-party data handling and privacy-incident escalation, in line with applicable privacy legislation such as BC’s Personal Information Protection Act.

Business intelligence, analytics and data governance

Deliver the BI and analytics plan with business owners, prioritizing dashboards, reporting and forecasting that support planning, operations, fundraising and community-impact decisions, measured by BI usage and data quality.

Oversee data architecture, integration and governance, setting ownership, quality and access standards that protect sensitive information.

Build data literacy through practical training so teams can use reports, shared definitions and reliable information in decisions and evaluation.

Projects and change

Lead cross-functional initiatives collaboratively, with clear executive sponsorship, business ownership, outcomes, scope, resources, milestones and success measures, delivering on time and cost.

Resolve competing operational, technical, financial, security and stakeholder needs, developing new approaches where existing practices fall short.

Co-design improvements with staff and business owners, leading readiness, process redesign, communication, training and post-launch support, sequenced to staff capacity to sustain adoption of new systems and tools.

Evaluate outcomes with business owners against agreed adoption, service, staff-time, data-quality, cost and risk measures, and recommend changes where benefits are not sustained.

People leadership

Lead integrated IT and BI functions, setting clear responsibilities, priorities, service expectations and performance objectives and allocating capacity across operations and initiatives.

Coach employees and leaders, and oversee recruitment, performance, engagement, development, succession and knowledge continuity.

Build an inclusive, collaborative, accountable and service-oriented culture and strong working relationships across UWBC, measured by team engagement and retention.

Financial and vendor management

Manage operating and capital budgets, project costs, capacity and funding needs, measured by budget performance against plan. Recommend significant investments and improve value from licensing, subscriptions and services.

Oversee vendors, consultants and managed services, including selection, contracts, renewals and performance, with corrective action where needed.

Ensure technology procurement and expenditures comply with organizational policies.

Qualifications and requirements: Education

University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Data/Analytics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant professional experience.

Advanced education or certification in technology governance, cybersecurity, data management, cloud or project management is an asset.

Experience

At least seven years of progressively responsible technology, digital or BI/data experience, including three years leading technology, data or multidisciplinary teams.

Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology, digital or data strategies and overseeing operations, cloud, applications, cybersecurity, technology risk, BI and data governance.

Demonstrated experience leading technology implementations and cross-functional change, including AI or automation, through staff engagement, process redesign, training and sustained adoption, with measurable benefits and safeguards.

Experience managing budgets, contracts, vendors and external service providers.

Assets: experience in complex, multi-location, nonprofit, public-sector or unionized environments; and experience integrating or deriving insight from CRM, financial or ERP systems and modern data platforms, such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI, Salesforce and Microsoft data warehouse technologies.

A key priority is enhancing its financial management, strategic planning, and reporting functions to support continued expansion, integration activities, and investor reporting.

Snowdon Partners

. This role represents a unique opportunity to build and lead a finance function in a growing private equity-backed business.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, working closely with the private equity CFO, and managing a team of four (4) direct reports, the Director of Finance serves as the company’s financial quarterback and is a key member of the leadership team, participating in strategic discussions and supporting all areas of the business.

Who You Are

The successful candidate is a hands-on accounting and finance leader with extensive experience in multi-currency, international consolidation and a strong track record of building scalable financial processes. You know that growth and management start with getting the basics right-timely, accurate reporting and robust controls – but you also understand that true financial leadership extends to driving strategy, supporting growth, and navigating complex international operations. You are energized by change, resilient in the face of challenges, and skilled at identifying which initiatives will deliver lasting impact.

You will dive into Nuvollo’s financial results, lead consolidation across multiple currencies and international entities, and work closely with the team to develop KPIs, reporting frameworks, best-in-class budgeting and forecasting tools. Your experience supporting acquisitions, integration initiatives, or international cross-selling efforts will allow you to contribute meaningfully to strategic growth opportunities as Nuvollo continues to scale. Manage the company’s financial accounts.
Identify, create, and implement financial controls.
Develop Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and create management dashboards to allow management to track performance of critical data points.
Prepare annual budgets and update with actual results throughout the year.
Prepare monthly and quarterly reporting packages, including year-to-date performance and projected year-end results.
Prepare compliance reports and financial packages for lender partners.
Become the “go-to” leader internally for financial performance data.

Ensure compliance with international accounting standards and local regulations in jurisdictions where Nuvollo operates.

Contribute financial integration support for acquisitions in new markets.

new_jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.
